title: Afghan Avalanche Rescue - Package, Long Version
description: Package made from "Afghan Avalanche Rescue" b-roll about coalition forces and Afghanistan security forces assisting Afghans injured in an avalanche in Parwan Province. Produced by Spc. Jennifer Dolsen
keywords: avalanche, Asif, Karen Kinne, Afghanistan, medical care

transcript.text: Afghan National Army and Coalition troops responded and organized rescue strategies
for Afghans affected by the avalanche in the area of Salang Tunnel, a main route that
connects Kabul to the eastern region of Afghanistan.
According to ISAF's Joint Command, more than 40 civilians were killed in the avalanche,
hundreds of displaced civilians were safely rescued by the Afghan National Army Air Corps
and ISAF air crews.
Many were flown to Bagram Airfield's Heath M. Craig Joint Theater Hospital and medically
triage based on the severity of their injuries.
Afghan doctor Mohammad Asif, a local doctor training with American doctors at Bagram,
says it's important for Afghans to lead the way in taking care of their country.
I want to be able to have a facility like the American Hospital here because I want
the help from my people, for our country, for anyone that's injured or ill.
Like many Afghan National doctors in the training program, Asif works closely with his
American counterparts in the emergency room to help injured.
Chief Nurse at the Hospital Air Force Colonel Karen Kinney explains the importance of the
joint environment.
I mean, this is where it all comes together.
It's pretty awesome to be able to have trained them up so that they're able to start seeing
the big picture of how to respond to emergencies.
We're here to serve the Afghans as best as we can and as you saw from the trauma bay, the
most critical ones, those that were in rollovers or were suffering from hypothermia, we were
able to provide a lot of intensive care and get them stabilized.
Colonel Kinney added the families of the injured are being kept as comfortable as possible in
other rooms of the hospital or at Bagram's recreation facility and are provided food,
water and warm clothes.
Specialist Jennifer Doulson, Bagram Airfield, Afghanistan.
